meaning: Where each ear meets his head: the ear is above the line, the head below.
how: v2: the outline over the top of the head is now pixel-precise (tools/ear_edges.py) and each base ends on a real notch of it. Ear (image right): follows its measured crease (median 0.76 px) from the notch where the dip rises (577.1, 272.0) to the notch near the crease's end on the outer side (715.8, 300.2). Ear (image left): no crease is visible (the v1 'faint crease' under the ledge was the ledge's own dark rim); the base takes the right ear's measured crease shape, mirrored, between the step-bottom notch (511.7, 279.3) and the corner below the little outward hook at the ear's outer base (371.6, 297.4), so the hook belongs to the ear (ears flare where they attach). INFERRED. v3: each ear includes everything down to where it meets the flat part of his head. Measured by averaging the brightness profile across each base along its length: on the ear on image right the v2 line sat in the bottom of the crease's groove; the surface keeps curving (brightness changing) until ~12-16 px lower, then is flat; the ear on image left flattens ~14 px lower. A brightness-slope map confirmed the curving band. Both lines lowered 12 px in the middle, easing (cosine, first 30%) to 0 at the inner corners, which already sit where the ears meet the flat dip; outer ends slid 12 px down along the outline: (363.0, 305.6) and (718.1, 312.4). Smooth (<3.5 deg over 2 px), inside the body. v4: v2 lowered 3 px (owner: ~3 px), easing to 0 at the inner corners; the ear on image right's outer end slid 3 px down the outline to (716.5, 303.1). The ear on image left's base flares outward below the hook: the outline runs straight at a steady -29 deg from the hook (371, 297) to (351.5, 311.8), where it starts curving as the head's side; that shaded flare is part of the ear's base, so the line's outer part sweeps down it (one cubic Hermite from x 440, no dip) to end there.
